features.title: F1: Pantry Board
features.body:
The main view. Shows what is in the pantry, what state each item is in, and separates current from expired.

**In scope:** two views (current, expired), item cards, status shown by color AND label, phone-width layout.
**Out of scope:** drag interaction (F2), photos.

**Constraint:** status must never be conveyed by color alone. Accessibility is a Definition of Done item, not a feature.

stories.title: Pantry Board: See my current pantry
stories.body:
**Pantry Board:** As a home cook, I want to see everything currently in my pantry on one board, so that I know what I have without opening a cabinet.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Each item shows name, quantity, storage location, and expiration date
- [ ] Board renders usably at phone width
- [ ] Empty pantry shows a first-run message pointing at the catalog
- [ ] Expired items do not appear in this view

tasks.title: Task: Base template and navigation shell
tasks.body:
- [ ] Page renders with a header and a content region
- [ ] Navigation between Current and Expired views
- [ ] Layout holds at 375px wide

tasks.title: Task: Pantry board view and URL
tasks.body:
- [ ] View queries current (non-expired) items
- [ ] URL routed and named
- [ ] Renders with zero items without erroring

tasks.title: Task: Item card partial
tasks.body:
- [ ] Shows name, quantity with unit, location, expiration date
- [ ] Long names wrap instead of breaking the layout
- [ ] Reused by both the current and expired views

tasks.title: Task: Empty state
tasks.body:
- [ ] Message when the pantry has no items
- [ ] Links directly to the catalog

tasks.title: Task: Tests for the pantry board view
tasks.body:
- [ ] Seeded items appear
- [ ] Expired items are excluded
- [ ] Empty pantry renders the empty state

stories.title: Pantry Board: See status at a glance
stories.body:
**Pantry Board:** As a home cook, I want each item to show its freshness status visually, so that I can spot what needs using without reading every date.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Fresh, expiring soon, and expired each have a distinct treatment
- [ ] Status is carried by a text label or icon as well as color
- [ ] The expiring-soon threshold is defined in one place, not in the template

tasks.title: Task: Item status classifier
tasks.body:
Single function or model property returning fresh / expiring_soon / expired.

- [ ] Threshold defined once as a setting, not hardcoded
- [ ] Boundary behavior explicit: what counts as the last fresh day, what counts as today
- [ ] Used by every view that needs status

tasks.title: Task: Status styling on the item card
tasks.body:
- [ ] Three visual states, distinguishable in grayscale
- [ ] Each carries a text label, not color alone

tasks.title: Task: Tests for status boundaries
tasks.body:
- [ ] Four days out is fresh
- [ ] Three days out is expiring soon
- [ ] Today and earlier is expired
- [ ] Item with no expiration date does not crash the classifier

stories.title: Pantry Board: See what has expired
stories.body:
**Pantry Board:** As a home cook, I want expired food in its own view, so that I don't plan a meal around something I need to throw out.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Separate view listing only expired items
- [ ] Reachable from the current pantry view and back
- [ ] Count of expired items is visible from the current view

tasks.title: Task: Expired view and URL
tasks.body:
- [ ] Queries only items past their expiration date
- [ ] Reuses the item card partial
- [ ] Empty state when nothing has expired

tasks.title: Task: Expired count indicator
tasks.body:
- [ ] Current view shows how many items have expired
- [ ] Indicator links to the expired view

tasks.title: Task: Tests for the expired view
tasks.body:
- [ ] Only expired items appear
- [ ] Count matches the number shown

features.title: F2: Add Items From Catalog
features.body:
Adding groceries must not be tedious. The user picks from a catalog of common supermarket items instead of typing every field.

**In scope:** seeded item catalog, search, click to add, quantity and date defaults.
**Out of scope for Sprint 1:** drag-and-drop, barcode scanning, photos.

**Decision:** click-to-add is the primary interaction. HTML5 drag-and-drop does not work on touch without a library and is not keyboard accessible, which conflicts with the phone-access requirement. Drag is an enhancement layered on later, not the only way in.

stories.title: Add Items: Browse a catalog of common groceries
stories.body:
**Add Items:** As a home cook, I want a ready-made list of common grocery items, so that I don't have to type out everything I bought.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Catalog is seeded with common supermarket items across major categories
- [ ] Each catalog entry carries a name, category, default unit, and default shelf life
- [ ] Catalog can be extended by loading more seed data without a code change

tasks.title: Task: CatalogItem model and migration
tasks.body:
- [ ] Fields: name, category, default_unit, shelf_life_days by storage location
- [ ] Field names match the agreed model contract
- [ ] Migration runs forward and back

tasks.title: Task: Seed the catalog with common groceries
tasks.body:
- [ ] Fixture or data migration with a solid starter set across produce, dairy, meat, pantry staples, frozen
- [ ] Shelf-life values sourced from a published food-safety reference, and the source noted
- [ ] Loading the seed twice does not create duplicates

tasks.title: Task: Catalog list view
tasks.body:
- [ ] Catalog renders grouped by category
- [ ] Usable at phone width
- [ ] Toggleable from the pantry board rather than always on screen

tasks.title: Task: Tests for catalog seeding and listing
tasks.body:
- [ ] Seed loads the expected number of entries
- [ ] Catalog view returns entries grouped by category

stories.title: Add Items: Search the catalog
stories.body:
**Add Items:** As a home cook, I want to search the catalog, so that I can find an item faster than scrolling a long list.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Search matches on partial item name, case-insensitive
- [ ] Matching items are shown at the top of the list
- [ ] No match shows a clear message rather than an empty screen

tasks.title: Task: Catalog search query
tasks.body:
- [ ] Case-insensitive partial name match
- [ ] Results ordered with matches first
- [ ] Blank search returns the full catalog, not nothing

tasks.title: Task: Search input on the catalog view
tasks.body:
- [ ] Input filters the catalog list
- [ ] Clearing the input restores the full list
- [ ] Works without JavaScript enabled, even if less smoothly

tasks.title: Task: Tests for catalog search
tasks.body:
- [ ] Partial match returns the expected entries
- [ ] Case differences still match
- [ ] No-match path returns an empty result cleanly

stories.title: Add Items: Add a catalog item to my pantry
stories.body:
**Add Items:** As a home cook, I want to click a catalog item to put it in my pantry, so that stocking groceries takes seconds.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] One action moves a catalog item into the pantry
- [ ] Expiration date is prefilled from the catalog shelf life and today's date
- [ ] Quantity defaults to 1 and the default unit comes from the catalog
- [ ] The new item appears on the pantry board immediately

### Notes
This is the walking skeleton. Catalog, database, board, and status classifier all get touched.

tasks.title: Task: PantryItem model and migration
tasks.body:
- [ ] Fields: catalog_item reference, custom name, quantity, unit, storage_location, added_on, expiration_date, removed_on, removal_reason
- [ ] Field names match the agreed model contract
- [ ] Migration runs forward and back

tasks.title: Task: Shelf-life date calculation
tasks.body:
- [ ] Expiration date derived from today plus the catalog shelf life for the chosen storage location
- [ ] Falls back sensibly when the catalog has no shelf life for that location
- [ ] Calculation lives in one place, reusable by later features

tasks.title: Task: Add-to-pantry view and route
tasks.body:
- [ ] Accepts a catalog item and creates a pantry item
- [ ] Rejects an unknown catalog id
- [ ] Redirects back to the board with the new item visible

tasks.title: Task: Add control on the catalog list
tasks.body:
- [ ] Each catalog row has a clear add action
- [ ] Action is reachable by keyboard and by touch
- [ ] Feedback confirms the item was added

tasks.title: Task: Tests for the add path
tasks.body:
- [ ] Adding a catalog item creates a pantry row with a calculated expiration date
- [ ] Unknown catalog id creates nothing
- [ ] Added item appears on the board

features.title: F3: Remove Items
features.body:
Items leave the pantry because they were eaten or because they went bad. Recording which is what makes waste reduction measurable.

**Decision:** removal is a soft delete with a reason (used or wasted), not a hard delete. Reducing waste is the stated point of the product, and a deleted row can never be counted. One extra column now, impossible to backfill later.

**Decision:** no confirmation dialog. Undo after the fact is less annoying and better understood than an are-you-sure prompt.

stories.title: Remove Items: Throw out or use up an item
stories.body:
**Remove Items:** As a home cook, I want to move an item to the trash when it's gone, so that my pantry stays true to what's actually there.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] One action removes an item from the board
- [ ] The action records whether it was used or wasted
- [ ] Removed items disappear from current and expired views
- [ ] The row is retained in the database, not deleted

tasks.title: Task: Soft-delete removal on PantryItem
tasks.body:
- [ ] Sets removed_on and removal_reason
- [ ] Default queryset excludes removed items
- [ ] Row is never hard-deleted

tasks.title: Task: Remove controls on the item card
tasks.body:
- [ ] Separate actions for used up and thrown out
- [ ] Reachable by keyboard and touch
- [ ] Board updates after the action

tasks.title: Task: Tests for removal
tasks.body:
- [ ] Removal sets the reason and hides the item from the board
- [ ] The underlying row still exists
- [ ] Removing an already-removed item does not error

features.title: F4: Edit Items
features.body: The pantry record drifts from reality unless the user can correct it. Quantity gets used down, dates get guessed wrong, things move from counter to fridge.

stories.title: Edit Items: Correct an item's details
stories.body:
**Edit Items:** As a home cook, I want to change an item's quantity, date, or location, so that a wrong guess doesn't make my whole pantry wrong.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Quantity, unit, storage location, and expiration date can all be changed
- [ ] Changing storage location offers to recalculate the expiration date
- [ ] Cancel leaves the item untouched

tasks.title: Task: Edit form for a pantry item
tasks.body:
- [ ] Prefilled with current values
- [ ] Validates date format and non-negative quantity
- [ ] Cancel returns to the board unchanged

tasks.title: Task: Edit view and route
tasks.body:
- [ ] Updates only submitted fields
- [ ] Returns 404 for an unknown or removed item
- [ ] Redirects to the board on success

tasks.title: Task: Tests for editing
tasks.body:
- [ ] Valid edit persists
- [ ] Invalid edit changes nothing and reports the error
- [ ] Editing a removed item is rejected

features.title: F5: AI Chef
features.body:
Turns an inventory into a decision about dinner. The Sprint 2 headline and the thing that makes this more than a list app.

**In scope:** recipe suggestions from current pantry contents, surfaced through a chef control on the board.
**Explicitly out of scope:** diet and nutrition recommendations. Different data, different product, and health advice from a language model is a liability we don't want in a demo.

**Risk:** API key handling, per-call cost, latency. Spike in Sprint 1.

stories.title: AI Chef: Decide how recipes get generated
stories.body:
**AI Chef:** As a team, we want a recorded decision on how recipe suggestions are produced, so that Sprint 2 starts building instead of debating.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Hosted LLM API, recipe database API, and hybrid each assessed
- [ ] Per-call cost, latency, and key handling documented for the chosen option
- [ ] Decision and reasoning recorded in this issue and linked from the README

tasks.title: Task: Compare recipe generation options
tasks.body:
- [ ] Three options assessed against cost, latency, and quality
- [ ] One recommended with reasons
- [ ] Written up in the issue

tasks.title: Task: Document API key handling
tasks.body:
- [ ] Where the key lives locally, in the devcontainer, and in CI
- [ ] Confirmed the key cannot reach the client or the repo
- [ ] Steps a teammate can follow without asking

features.title: F6: Delivery Pipeline
features.body:
How work gets from a branch to the shared product without breaking it. Enabling work, not a vertical slice, and that is fine. Covers the Definition of Done items nobody else owns: integration, automated verification, review, defect tracking, decisions recorded.

**Note:** the Django project lives in `project/`, not the repo root. Every CI step and every README command needs that working directory or it will not find manage.py.

stories.title: Delivery Pipeline: Verify the devcontainer and starter
stories.body:
**Delivery Pipeline:** As a developer, I want the devcontainer to build and the app to run from documented steps, so that nobody loses a day to setup.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Devcontainer builds from a clean clone
- [ ] Migrations run and the dev server serves a page
- [ ] pytest runs and passes
- [ ] Steps are in the README and reproduced by a second teammate

tasks.title: Task: Build the devcontainer from a clean clone
tasks.body:
- [ ] Container builds with no manual fixes
- [ ] Dependencies from requirements.txt install
- [ ] Migrations run and the server starts

tasks.title: Task: Confirm pytest configuration works
tasks.body:
- [ ] pytest discovers and runs tests
- [ ] Django settings module resolves correctly
- [ ] A deliberately failing test actually fails the run

tasks.title: Task: Write setup steps in the README
tasks.body:
- [ ] Exact commands in order, copy-pasteable
- [ ] Notes that commands run from project/
- [ ] Environment variables listed

tasks.title: Task: Second teammate reproduces setup
tasks.body:
- [ ] Another member follows the README from scratch
- [ ] Anything that tripped them up is fixed in the README

stories.title: Delivery Pipeline: Run tests on every pull request
stories.body:
**Delivery Pipeline:** As a developer, I want tests to run automatically on every pull request, so that broken code can't reach main.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Workflow installs, migrates, and runs pytest on PRs to main
- [ ] Workflow runs from the project directory
- [ ] A deliberately failing test blocks the merge
- [ ] Only changes under project/ trigger the run

tasks.title: Task: CI workflow for install, migrate, pytest
tasks.body:
- [ ] Triggers on pull requests to main
- [ ] working-directory set to project/
- [ ] Path filter so lab commits elsewhere in the repo do not trigger it
- [ ] Finishes in under five minutes

tasks.title: Task: Require the CI check before merge
tasks.body:
- [ ] Branch protection on main requires the check
- [ ] Direct pushes to main blocked

tasks.title: Task: Prove a failing test blocks the merge
tasks.body:
- [ ] Throwaway PR with a failing test is blocked
- [ ] Evidence linked on the story issue

stories.title: Delivery Pipeline: Agree a Definition of Done
stories.body:
**Delivery Pipeline:** As a team, we want an agreed Definition of Done, so that done means the same thing to all five of us.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Draft posted as a pinned issue
- [ ] Every member has acknowledged it
- [ ] Checklist reflected in the story issue template
- [ ] Includes: works at phone width, and status is never conveyed by color alone

tasks.title: Task: Draft and pin the DoD issue
tasks.body:
- [ ] Covers criteria met, integrated, tests pass in CI, reviewed, no blocking defects, decisions recorded
- [ ] Includes the accessibility line
- [ ] Pinned in the repo

tasks.title: Task: Collect team acknowledgement
tasks.body:
- [ ] All five members have responded
- [ ] Requested changes folded in

stories.title: Delivery Pipeline: Story and bug issue templates
stories.body:
**Delivery Pipeline:** As a team, we want story and bug templates with a criteria checklist, so that work starts with criteria instead of guesses.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Story template prompts for the feature name and the As a / I want / so that line
- [ ] Bug template prompts for steps, expected, actual, severity
- [ ] New issues open prefilled

tasks.title: Task: Story issue template
tasks.body:
- [ ] Prompts for feature name and the story sentence
- [ ] Acceptance criteria checklist
- [ ] DoD checklist included

tasks.title: Task: Bug issue template
tasks.body:
- [ ] Steps to reproduce, expected, actual
- [ ] Severity field with blocking called out
